adopted_campaign_rules: A resolved cast consumes exactly one prepared/fetched copy and its matching slot, once. Knowledge/access is not a cast.
At most one spell or active magical power per actor per round, subject to casting time; familiars cannot supply extra caster actions.

After casting a spell of level 3 or higher, that caster must complete two intervening rounds before another level-3-or-higher cast. This is a campaign house rule, not an AD&D 2e default. Lower-level magic and ordinary actions remain possible.
Snogard keeps at most six fetched copies, at most one copy per named spell. The persisted cache is a campaign retention exception; it is never refreshed by a turn, sheet view, reload or encounter.
Gene fetches one spell at a time; fetch duration and risk resolve in game time. A spent Fireball cannot be used again until a new authorized retrieval succeeds and the recovery rule permits it.
Preparation needs actual rest/prayer/study and recorded resources. Level-up or maintenance never fills slots or restores spent magic.
Unknown item charges, companion spellcasting and custom effects grant zero executable uses until a definition is approved. Passive documented gear remains usable under its rules.
No blanket anti-magic or fabricated enemy immunity. Telegraph observed hazards, allow saves and counters, account for friendly fire, flammable belongings, confined space and relevant components.
NPCs preserve scarce magic when ordinary tactics can work; offer costly magical solutions with an explicit benefit and consequence. Snogard choices always belong to the player.

Gene Emberlight and Sekhem Serpent Ward are new finite campaign grants, each one initial use and at most 1/day thereafter. They share Snogard’s magic-action budget, require explicit permission, and replenish only after resolved rest with a recorded reset. They never refresh priest preparations or fetched spells.
